Place names: labels, their areas, the Find box and what is known of each

Source: R/names.R
og_names.Rd

og_names() writes a list of place names on the map, each from its own zoom, the larger names first where they meet; the page's Find box looks through them (accents aside), and a click on a name, or a name found, shows its row. Where the names have areas, these are a layer of their own, off when the page opens, a click inside one showing the same.

Usage

og_names(
  map = NULL,
  names = NULL,
  colour = "#0b3954",
  early = 0,
  areas = FALSE,
  popup = NULL,
  open = FALSE,
  name = "Place names",
  id = "names",
  info = NULL,
  section = "Reference",
  visible = TRUE
)

Arguments

map

A map the pipe makes (og_map(), with data or none, and any layer functions). Given the names instead (or nothing), a map is started for them.

names

The place names (see The list of names).

colour

The names' colour when the page opens, "#rrggbb"; the page offers dark blue (the default), black, white, red and yellow.

early

How many zooms before its own each name appears when the page opens: -1 (a zoom later), 0, 1 or 2; the page has the same choice.

areas

Whether the names' areas show when the page opens.

popup

The columns a click shows, by name; by default every column but the name's place, zoom, rank, n and area.

open

Whether the layer's controls show when the page opens; folded by default.

name, info

The layer's name in the sidebar (the areas' is "Areas of the names") and the text behind its ⓘ.

id

The layer's id, its key in the page's address; the areas' is <id>_areas.

section

The sidebar's box the layers sit in, by its title.

visible

Whether the names are on when the page opens.

Value

The map, with the layers.

Details

The arguments are the starting look; the page's controls, folded under ▸ beside the layer's name, change the names' colour and the zoom they appear at.

The list of names

names is a table with a row for each name (a name of several places, a row for each), one of:

  • nothing (NULL): the file named by the environment variable OGIS_NAMES, a line in .Renviron (OGIS_NAMES=D:/data/ornefni.parquet), so a script shared between colleagues carries no path;

  • the path of a (Geo)Parquet file; or of a GeoPackage, GeoJSON or any file sf reads;

  • a data frame, an sf object, or a lazy table on DuckDB.

Its columns, all but name optional:

  • name: the name, as written on the map and found;

  • label_lon, label_lat (or lon, lat): where the name is written; else on its area;

  • a geometry column (geometry, geom): the name's area, a line or a point, drawn as the layer <id>_areas;

  • min_zoom: the zoom the name shows from (every zoom where it is missing);

  • level: its rank, 1 to 4, 1 the largest: the text's size, and the order names are placed in where they meet;

  • n: within a rank, the larger placed first (how often a name is used, say);

  • the others: what a click shows, labelled by the file's data dictionary (data-dict.tidyverse.org's, in the Parquet file's metadata), else by their names.

See also

og_text() and og_polygon(), which draw them, for labels and areas of your own.

Examples

# four names, each from its own zoom
places <- data.frame(
  name = c("Skagen", "Hirtshals", "Frederikshavn", "Læsø"),
  lon = c(10.59, 9.96, 10.54, 11.0), lat = c(57.72, 57.59, 57.44, 57.27),
  min_zoom = c(5, 6, 6, 5), level = c(1, 2, 2, 1),
  kind = c("town", "harbour", "harbour", "island")
)
og_names(places)
#> <og_map> Map
#>   layers: names (geojson)

# a list of names named once, by OGIS_NAMES in .Renviron:
# og_map() |> og_relief() |> og_names()
